text:
IncidentBot: :rotating_light: SEV-1 alert — Cassio (enterprise VPC) experiencing sudden prefix KV cache hit-rate collapse in us-west-2 dedicated pool. Created INC-2189102468. Auto-page SRE oncall.

Alex: I'm seeing prefix hit-rate drop from ~88% to 6% for tenant cassio-tenant-4, token error spike + tail latency jumps. Grafana: https://grafana.redwood.internal/d/kv-prefetch/tenant-cassio (link)

Tom: acknowledged, taking lead. Oncall here — will triage. @Priya you free to assist?

Priya: joining. Quick look at kv-proxy metrics: backend miss rate up 12x, prefix churn high. KV cache size for tenant is 4x normal; many short-lived prefixes. Looks like cache pollution from noisy prefixes.

JP: from runtime side, this pattern smells like uncontrolled client-side prefix expansion / bad prefetch heuristics. Could be a bot client or new rollout at Cassio generating high prefix variety.

Sara: Cassio ops pinged support — reporting 20% request failures and UI slowdowns for key flows since ~09:12 UTC. They're on standby.

Liam: can we throttle prefetch for that tenant or apply per-tenant caps? Prefer soft mitigations first (rate limit prefetch + reduce TTL).

Alex: I'm going to try temporary prefetch rate cap and a denylist for the top noisy prefixes to buy time. Will run in staging then apply.

Alex: running command to set prefetch cap:
```
curl -s -X POST https://api.redwood.internal/cache/control \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $ADMIN_TOKEN" \
  -d '{"action":"set_prefetch_policy","tenant":"cassio-tenant-4","prefetch_rate_per_s":30,"prefetch_ttl_s":10}'
```

IncidentBot: Action logged: prefetch policy change requested by Alex.

Priya: adding denylist for top noisy prefixes (pfx-089, pfx-zzz) to stop them from occupying KV cache.

Priya: command I ran (kv-admin):
```
kv-admin --tenant cassio-tenant-4 prefix deny add pfx-089 pfx-zzz pfx-temp
```

Alex: after policy + denylist: tenant hit-rate improved from 6% -> 47% in ~60s. Error rate down ~65%. Latency tail reduced but still above SLO.

Tom: good improvement. Need to minimize blast radius and make this durable. Short term mitigations applied: prefetch cap, denylist, restart prefetch worker for tenant.

Liam: note — restart caused brief 503s for 12s due to warmup (expected). Communicated to Cassio support.

SupportBot: Cassio ops acknowledged mitigation and confirmed reduced failures in their dashboard.

JP: next steps — require runtime changes: per-tenant LRU isolation, prefetch rate enforcement at proxy, and telemetry to detect prefix storms earlier. I'll open an engineering ticket and tag eng-runtime.

Tom: assigning follow-ups:
- JP: eng runtime fix (per-tenant isolation + caps) — P1 ticket ENG-2381
- Priya: refine denylist + automations to derive denylist from prefix entropy — runbook update
- Alex: coordinate with Cassio ops for root-cause (client rollout?) and collect request samples
- Support: open customer incident with Cassio and request logs + recent deploys

Sara: capturing CI/CD window — Cassio reported they did a service push at 09:05 UTC. Could correlate.

Priya: adding quick runbook snippet to this thread for oncall:
```
# Quick mitigations for tenant prefix storm
1) set prefetch cap: POST /cache/control set_prefetch_policy
2) apply denylist: kv-admin prefix deny add <prefixes>
3) restart prefetch worker: systemctl restart prefetcher@<tenant>
4) monitor hit-rate and tail latency
```

Tom: I'll be primary incident owner for postmortem. JP, please escalate to eng-runtime and include perf traces + flamegraphs.

Alex: created internal incident ticket INC-2189102468 and linked ENG-2381. Noting recovery window started 09:18 UTC.

IncidentBot: Incident status updated → mitigated. Severity lowered to SEV-2.

Priya: preliminary RCA hypothesis: client-side release at Cassio created extreme prefix variance, which overwhelmed prefetch heuristics causing cache pollution and global eviction pressure in the dedicated pool.

Tom: action items and owners documented. Postmortem owner: Tom. Target postmortem draft by EOD tomorrow.

Sara: closing communication to Cassio — they want follow-up call. I'll schedule business-hours bridge.

Alex: final note — consider adding automated protective defaults (hard caps + denylist auto-generation) for enterprise tenants on Dedicated pools to avoid cross-tenant impact.

Liam: +1 for defaults. Also track quota burn when prefetch restored.

Tom: thanks everyone. Marking thread resolved for now. :white_check_mark:
